operations.title: Carry the Load through the Canal
Register a Load on the Disrupted Route

initialSignals.description: A dock worker is asking for careful readers of the shipping register. Your Crew can investigate the record and compare the tide ledger.
initialSignals.title: A dock worker wants a quiet word

initialSignals.description: Your Family controls the route, but available wire cannot cover a complete shipment response. Gather a runner, a crafted route seal and the missing supplies to protect it.
initialSignals.title: Your dock shipment needs protection

initialSignals.description: The shipping register confirms a contested opportunity. Your Family can gather a runner, a crafted route seal and wire to intercept the load.
initialSignals.title: The rival dock route is vulnerable

initialSignals.description: Independent tide and survey evidence confirm a canal passage. Two members of your Crew can move the load with less wire and avoid an attack.
initialSignals.title: Your Crew found a quiet crossing

initialSignals.description: The protection operation kept the route under Family control. Restore its working supply line with a runner, a route seal and wire.
initialSignals.title: The Family holds the dock

initialSignals.description: The dock stayed under its controller. Workers are waiting for the route to reopen.
initialSignals.title: The Family holds the dock

initialSignals.description: The interception changed control of the route. The new holders must organize repairs before the captured supply line can settle.
initialSignals.title: The dock has changed hands

initialSignals.description: A different Family now holds the dock route. The captured supply line needs repairs.
initialSignals.title: The dock has changed hands

initialSignals.description: The verified canal route avoided a direct attack and used less wire. Members of one Crew can now maintain the crossing and secure its future.
initialSignals.title: A Crew opened the canal crossing

initialSignals.description: A Crew found another way through the docks. The canal passage now needs maintenance.
initialSignals.title: A Crew opened the canal crossing

initialSignals.description: Your Family's load is stranded behind a blocked dock route. Recover the depot, or compare the dispatch records and reopen supplies to the neighborhood. Bring a runner, a stamped cargo seal and wire.
initialSignals.title: The Missing Shipment

initialSignals.description: The shipping register identifies a stranded depot. Intercept its route or destroy the depot before another Family moves. Supplies held for an attempt can be reclaimed if you cancel before carrying it out.
initialSignals.title: A stranded shipment can change hands

initialSignals.description: The dock register has an unfinished dispatch. Read the route instructions and compare the surviving records before deciding what happened.
initialSignals.title: A dispatch did not get through

information.stakes: Recovery can fail and cost your supplied equipment. A successful interception changes who controls the route.
information.whyKnown: Your Family controls the registered depot and knows its shipping instructions.

information.stakes: Another Family may reach the depot before you.
information.whyKnown: You have verified notes from the depot register.

information.stakes: The unfinished dispatch is a lead, not proof of theft.
information.whyKnown: Your Crew is near the dock register.

initialSignals.description: The diverted depot cut off the registered supply route. A Family can open an alternate market here with its own stamped seals and wire.
initialSignals.title: The Black Market

information.stakes: The first Family to open the stalls controls the market route. It must still bring its own supplies.
information.whyKnown: Your shipping instructions identify this depot.

initialSignals.description: Bring supplies to the market, seize its route, expose its activity, or rebuild the registered supply line. Each plan needs a stamped cargo seal, a runner and wire from your own stores.
initialSignals.title: The canal market needs a decision

initialSignals.description: The canal depot is operating as an alternate market. Its suppliers and private plans remain unknown.
initialSignals.title: A market opened beside the canal

information.stakes: Supplied wire stays with the depot. Exposing the market makes its route public and leaves a paper trail.
information.whyKnown: You know the depot instructions and can identify the market route.

information.stakes: You can see the stalls, but their suppliers and private arrangements remain unknown.
information.whyKnown: The depot has opened for trade.

initialSignals.description: Someone knew the market route. The notice you examined is one public source, not proof of betrayal. Secure the records, compare independent evidence, or publish a disputed allegation with its uncertainty preserved.
initialSignals.title: The Informant

initialSignals.description: Two readers independently examined the posted notice and printer copy. Your Crew can document how the route became public without naming anyone guilty.
initialSignals.title: Two independent records explain the disclosure

initialSignals.description: The market's exposure left a notice at the docks. Read it and compare the surviving records before accepting any accusation.
initialSignals.title: The exposed market left a paper trail

information.stakes: An uncorroborated allegation consumes supplies and leaves a disputed record; it establishes no player guilt.
information.whyKnown: You examined the posted notice, or an investigator shared their verified notes with you.

information.stakes: The public paper trail can explain this disclosure without accusing anyone of betrayal.
information.whyKnown: A different investigator corroborated your evidence.

information.stakes: Different readers may know different parts of the evidence.
information.whyKnown: Your local Crew can inspect the visible notice.

initialSignals.description: Your Family's recent operations have gone badly, and this load is still stranded. Someone who joined the failed recovery must examine its report before a new plan is agreed. None of this proves betrayal.
initialSignals.title: The Informant: a failed plan

information.stakes: Someone who joined the failed recovery must bring its verified report. The report establishes no one's guilt.
information.whyKnown: You belong to the depot-controlling Family and know its route.

metadata.title: The Tide Ledger
metadata.description: The old tide ledger describes a shallow canal crossing. A second survey must verify its clearance.

metadata.title: The Survey Plate
metadata.description: A crafted route seal fits the survey plate and exposes the clearance measurement. An independent tide record can confirm a peaceful crossing.

metadata.title: The Family Holds the Dock
metadata.description: The route records who acted and which materials were spent. Its new condition creates the next local decision.

metadata.title: The Dock Changes Hands
metadata.description: The route records who acted and which materials were spent. Its new condition creates the next local decision.

metadata.title: The Crew Opens a Quiet Passage
metadata.description: The route records who acted and which materials were spent. Its new condition creates the next local decision.

metadata.title: The Dispatch Register
metadata.description: Compare the dock dispatch records when a shipment needs attention. An incomplete entry alone is not proof of theft or interference.

metadata.title: The Cargo Seal Impressions
metadata.description: Your stamped seal matches the registered depot impressions. The shipping instructions show how a Crew can reopen the neighborhood supply route.

metadata.title: The Dock Noticeboard
metadata.description: Check the dock noticeboard for shipping papers you can examine. A public posting may explain a rumor; it is not proof of betrayal.

metadata.title: The Printer Copy
metadata.description: The seal authenticates a matching copy of the public notice. An independent reader can corroborate public disclosure; neither copy proves internal betrayal.

metadata.title: Your Shipping Records
metadata.description: Keep your shipping notes here. If you took part in a job, compare its papers; another person's private report belongs in their own notebook.

metadata.title: Your Part in the Disclosure
metadata.description: You participated in disclosing this market route. Your report records that action. Whether the disclosure was authorized is not established, and participation alone does not prove betrayal.

metadata.title: Review a Recovery Plan
metadata.description: If you took part in an unsuccessful recovery, examine its report before changing the plan. An unsuccessful plan alone does not establish betrayal.
